evidence.r1: The Up next track list is a large glass content panel, not just a navigation or transport control.
evidence.r2: The glass playlist menu opens directly on top of the glass Up next panel.
evidence.r3: Transport, volume, queue and its temporary playlist menu are few and functionally relevant.
evidence.r4: The transport, volume, queue and playlist menu share one pale frosted material appearance.
evidence.r5: No clear variant is visible; substantial pale frosting covers the ice artwork behind the controls.
evidence.r6: The scrubber has a red filled segment even though it is not the primary playback action.
evidence.r7: The normal transport and queue reveal softened ice variation that disappears in the reduced-transparency capture.
evidence.r8: The main surfaces use fixed rounded rectangles and the playback selection is circular.
evidence.r9: The playlist menu focus row has tighter corner arcs than the enclosing menu inset implies.
evidence.r10: The compact menu rows use rounded rectangles, and the prominent playback control is circular.
evidence.r11: Transport items share one surface, volume has its own group, and queue actions live with the queue.
evidence.r12: Transport buttons are icons and playlist actions are labelled rows, with no separate text-button and icon-button mixture.
evidence.r13: Glass is applied to the whole transport and volume controls rather than their icons or slider thumbs.
evidence.r14: The playlist menu and queue overlap as two distinct material sheets rather than one joined container.
evidence.r15: No scroll-edge treatment is visible for the queue or album region beneath floating controls.
evidence.r16: Every floating surface sits over the detailed full-window ice artwork.
evidence.r17: The album heading and track list start below the transport and remain to the left of the queue.
evidence.r18: The pale transport is readable, but no dark appearance establishes the required contrast in both modes.
evidence.r19: Reduced transparency preserves the transport and queue, but increased contrast and reduced-motion behaviour are not shown.
evidence.r20: Ice artwork reaches all four window edges behind floating transport, volume and queue.
evidence.r21: Album content clears the top transport and right queue while the ice background continues seamlessly beneath both.
evidence.r22: The material surfaces sit directly over continuous artwork without separate backing strips or added local scrims.
evidence.r23: The playlist menu is only shown fully open, so its morph and pointer feedback cannot be determined.
evidence.r24: The transport scrubber introduces a red accent into otherwise monochrome control content.
evidence.r25: Dark album-track controls sit directly over dark blue-grey ice fissures of similar colour.
